elements.id-string-9: \abstract{We introduce a new discretization based on the Trefftz-DG method for solving the Stokes equations.Discrete solutions of a corresponding method fulfill the Stokes equation pointwise within each element and yield element-wise divergence-free solutions.
elements.id-string-10: Compared to standard DG methods, a strong reduction of the degrees of freedom is achieved, especially for higher order polynomial degrees.
elements.id-string-11: In addition, in contrast to many other Trefftz-DG methods, our approach allows to easily incorporate inhomogeneous right hand sides (driving forces) by using the concept of the embedded Trefftz-DG method.On top of a detailed a priori error analysis, we furthercompare our approach to standard discontinuous Galerkin Stokes discretizations and present numerical examples.}

elements.id-string-40: \paragraph*{Main contributions and structure of the manuscript}
elements.id-string-41: In this work we extend the (embedded) Trefftz-DG methodology to the Stokes problem.
elements.id-string-42: We introduce a DG method with local basis functions that are polynomials and solve the Stokes problem pointwise.
elements.id-string-43: This extends the approach introduced in \cite{montlaur2010discontinuous,montlaur08} where a DG method using element-wise divergence-free polynomials is presented for the Stokes and Navier-Stokes equations.
elements.id-string-44: In view of the Trefftz methodology the approach in \cite{montlaur2010discontinuous,montlaur08} can be seen as a Trefftz-DG method with respect to the mass conservation equation, while the Trefftz-DG discretization considered in this paper includes also the momentum equation in the construction of the Trefftz-DG space.
elements.id-string-45: The analysis of the discretization reveals that higher order pressure functions are locally determined by the velocity and that only the piecewise constant pressures appear as Lagrange multipliers in the Stokes saddle point problem.
elements.id-string-46: We prove stability of the saddle point problem and derive a priori error bounds in the energy as well as the $L^2$ norm of the velocity.
elements.id-string-47: In contrast to most other works on Trefftz-DG methods we allow inhomogeneous right hand side source terms in the method and its analysis.
elements.id-string-48: While the method for treating inhomogeneous right hand sides has already been introduced in \cite{2201.07041}, to the best of our knowledge, this is the first time a rigorous error analysis is provided for this generic approach in dealing with inhomogenities.

elements.id-string-732: Comparison of computational effort to different Stokes discretizations
elements.id-string-733: In this section we want to compare the Trefftz-DG method with other popular discretizations for the Stokes problem with respect to the number of unknowns and their sparsity patterns that finally determine the computational costs to a large extend.
elements.id-string-734: For a comparison we only consider simplicial meshes and mostly restrict to different variants of DG methods.
elements.id-string-735: We include several hybrid Discontinuous Galerkin (HDG) methods, where the velocity couplings across element interfaces stemming from DG-terms are avoided by introducing additional facet unknowns for the velocities.
elements.id-string-736: As an exception we also include the Taylor-Hood method (of arbitrary high order) which has continuous velocity and pressure approximations.
elements.id-string-737: The list of methods presented here is by no means complete, for additional material on HDG methods we refer to e.g. \cite{zbMATH05837531,COCKBURN2014221,L_MTH_2010}, and for further exploration we refer to the relevant literature, including the books \cite{di2011mathematical,brezzi,zbMATH06625569} and the references therein.
